newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden says Stadshypotek bids take time.
newsitem.headline: Sweden says Stadshypotek bids take time.

text.p: Sweden's finance department has received a handful of bids for the auction of its 34 percent stake in mortgage bank Stadshypotek but the process will take time, a departmental spokeswoman said on Monday.
"The faxes are still warm," spokeswoman Barbara Ericsson told Reuters. "It cannot take more than a certain number of pages at any one time.
"All the bids have yet to come in but we have received a handful," she said.
The Swedish state announced nine days ago that it planned to sell its stake in Stadshypotek to an industrial buyer through a controlled auction.
Ericsson said no information will be released today about the bid as it would take time.
She said she would go to London to talk to investment banking advisers Merrill Lynch about the bid.
"It is a complicated process to value the bid, to look at what they want to pay with shares, cash or if they want to buy only the 34 percent or the whole company."
Since the government announced the auction, Stadshypotek and insurer Skandia have announced a proposed merger.
But Finance Minister Erik Asbrink has voiced strong opposition to way the proposal was announced, saying he was not consulted.
